newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan suspends exchange visits with Iran.
newsitem.headline: Japan suspends exchange visits with Iran.

text.p: Japan is suspending exchange visits by government officials with Iran after a German court accused Tehran of ordering the killing of Kurdish dissidents in Berlin, Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda said on Tuesday.
But Japan will not recall its ambassador to Iran, Ikeda told a news conference.
"The international community has been in agreement to demand that Iran cut ties with terrorists. But the method of bringing this about is different from country to country," Ikeda said.
"Our country is suspending high-level exchanges while at the same time keeping open a channel of dialogue," he said.

Germany ordered four Iranian diplomats out of the country and recalled its ambassador in Tehran after last Thursday's verdict, which found the Iranian leadership was behind the killing of four Kurdish dissidents in 1992.
Iran denied the accusations and retaliated by expelling four German diplomats in Iran and recalling its ambassador to Bonn.
The European Union endorsed Germany's stance and invited members to follow Germany's lead in recalling ambassadors.
Japan, which buys about 10 percent of its total crude oil imports from Iran, has always distanced itself from sanctions against Iran.

Last August, Japan criticised the United States for enacting a law requiring sanctions against firms, including foreign ones, that invest $40 million or more a year in oil and gas projects in Iran or Libya.
